correctness.rationale: Each small cell is an incidence of an original edge with one of its two incident faces. A contact is at an old endpoint or in the same large face; in the latter case the original edges also share an endpoint. Hence the graph is L(2T), with a 12-clique at every old vertex. The even-order Cayley graph meets Abdollahi's exact hypotheses: its abelian group splits into a nontrivial 2-group and an odd-order group, and the generators connect it. Six 1-factors color the single edges and can be used with disjoint palettes on the parallel copies. For odd order, the proof's induced-edge bounds check at s=3,5 by simplicity, s=7 by the induced neighbor hexagon or degree at most five, s=9,11 by the nonzero even cut, and s≥13 by six-regularity. The six neighbors induce exactly the ordinary hexagon: differences between local representatives cannot match a generator only by wrapping, as m,n≥5. This gives odd density at most 13 and the full odd vertex set gives density greater than 12. Goldberg–Seymour and the matching lower bound agree. The planar coloring uses the two parities along the lines in each of three directions, with a separate color for each of the two face sides.
residual_risks: The finite replay establishes a witness at 5×5 only. The general result, including all even cases, depends on the analytic argument, and the stated contact identification is restricted to the given tiling and periods.

originality.rationale: The exact parity classification is mechanically implied by the already identified contact-graph model and standard theorems. In the odd case Mader's theorem supplies a stronger cut bound than the frozen family-specific density estimate. For any connected simple d-regular vertex-transitive graph G of odd order N, every proper odd S has at least d edges in its cut, so the density of 2G on S is (2d|S|−2|δ_G(S)|)/(|S|−1)≤2d. The full set has density 2dN/(N−1)>2d (for d>0); the matching bound and Goldberg–Seymour give chi'(2G)=ceil(2dN/(N−1)). The quotient in the finding is immediately such a graph with d=6 and N≥25. For even order Abdollahi's theorem already gives the needed 1-factorization from the displayed group and connectivity, and doubling the colors is immediate. The exact named toroidal wording need not have appeared previously for this coverage to hold; no priority chronology is inferred from same-day records.
residual_risks: An earlier publication of this exact toroidal wording was not established. Same-day catalogue chronology remains unresolved; neither issue affects the demonstrated mathematical implication.
